title: Mint chocolate chip ice cream
summary: A dairy-free coconut base steeped with fresh mint, sharpened with peppermint and streaked with fine chocolate flecks.
steps: Bring the coconut cream and coconut milk to a simmer, add the mint, take off the heat, cover and steep 30 minutes. Strain, pressing the leaves, and return the liquid to the pan.
Reheat until steaming. Whisk the yolks, allulose and salt, slowly whisk in the hot coconut, then return to the pan and stir over low heat until it reaches 80 °C (176 °F) and coats a spatula.
Strain, stir in the peppermint extract, and chill at least 4 hours.
Melt both chocolates with the coconut oil and let it cool until barely warm but still fluid.
Churn the base. In the last minute of churning, drizzle the chocolate in a thin stream into the machine; it freezes into crisp flecks. Freeze 3–4 hours before serving.
tips: Steeping fresh mint gives a grassier, rounder flavour than extract alone; the extract adds the cool finish.
Fresh-mint ice cream is pale cream, not green; that is the honest colour.

origin.history: Mint-flavoured ices are old, but mint chocolate chip as a named flavour is often credited to a British culinary student's entry in a 1973 competition to create a dish for the wedding of Princess Anne. It became one of the most popular ice-cream flavours in Britain and North America.
